newsitem.title: CHINA: China Typhoon Sally death toll rises to 162.
newsitem.headline: China Typhoon Sally death toll rises to 162.

text.p: The death toll from Typhoon Sally, which battered southern China earlier this week, has risen to 162, official media said on Friday.

The typhoon had injured more than 5,000 and flattened more than 272,000 houses when it raged across southern Guangdong province on Monday and sliced into neighbouring Guangxi region the next day, the China Daily said.
It said 50 people were still missing.
The storm's rains and 175-kph (110-mph) winds had damaged 680,000 hectares (1.68 million acres) of crops and knocked out communications and road links in the region, it said.
The Ministry of Civil Affairs estimated the typhoon had affected about 150 million people, it said.
In Guangdong, the storm killed 123 people, injured more than 4,300 and damaged 181,000 homes, it said.
Heavy rains and strong winds had continued to lash Guangxi after the typhoon passed, the China news service said.
The storms had killed 39 people in Guangxi, sunk more than 300 boats and affected more than 900,000 people, it said.
The typhoon came on the heels of devastating floods that swept across central and southern China in July, killing at least 2,700 people and leaving hundreds of thousands homeless.
